We have **Sennheiser XS Wireless 2** sets: an **SK-XSW bodypack transmitter** (clips on the belt, mic plugs in) and an
**EM-XSW 2 receiver** (the box with two antennas, cabled to the mixer). Each receiver listens to one frequency, and the
bodypack sends on whatever frequency the receiver gave it.

Page numbers below are from Sennheiser's *XS Wireless Series* instruction manual (v1.1, 05/2026). It covers the XSW 1 and the XSW 2.

## The problem

When two receivers sit on frequencies that are too close, receiver 1 also picks up pack 2, and you hear the wrong person
(or both people) on one channel. Sennheiser's rule for running more than one system (p. 57):

> "Only the factory-preset transmission frequencies within one frequency bank are intermodulation-free."
> "Set the same channel bank for all receivers. Assign one channel from this channel bank to each receiver."

So the fix is to put **both receivers in the same bank, on different channels**, and then sync each pack to its own receiver.
Close frequencies usually come from a manual TUNE, two separate scans that ended up near each other, or two different banks.

## Before you start

- **Both systems must be the same frequency range** (p. 77). The letter is in the set's name, e.g. XSW 2-ME2-**A**. Check the
  labels on the receiver and the pack; I haven't checked where the label shows it. Ranges (p. 81): A 548–572, GB 606–630,
  B 614–638, C 630–662, BC 670–694, D 766–790 MHz (and others). If your two sets are **different** ranges, they can't land on the
  same frequency, so the problem is something else (see [Still crosstalk?](#still-crosstalk)).
- Each XSW 2 range has **8 banks of up to 12 preset channels** (p. 81).
- Menu keys on the receiver (p. 49): **UP / DOWN** moves, **SET** opens or saves, **ON/OFF** is Escape (cancel).
- Label the receivers and packs **1** and **2** with tape so they don't get mixed up.

## Fix 1: same bank, different channels (fastest)

Do it on **receiver 1**, then on **receiver 2**:

1. Press UP/DOWN until the display shows **PRESET**, then press **SET** (p. 51).
2. Pick the **bank** with UP/DOWN and press **SET**. Use the **same bank number on both receivers**.
3. Pick the **channel** with UP/DOWN and press **SET**. Receiver 1 gets channel 1 and receiver 2 gets channel 2 (any two different
   channels in that bank will do).
4. **Sync the pack** (the frequency is stored only in the receiver until you sync, pp. 51–53, 77–78):
   - Switch the matching bodypack on and hold it near its receiver.
   - **Press and hold SYNC on the bodypack**. Its LED flashes red and green.
   - While it flashes, **short-press SYNC on the receiver**.
   - When the pack's LED turns steady green, the pair is linked (pp. 66, 79). The pack's display shows the bank, channel and frequency (p. 74).
5. Check: the pack's display and the receiver's display should show the same bank and channel.

Sync on these units goes over 2.4 GHz radio, not infrared (p. 81), so the two only need to be near each other. Do one pair at a
time, with the other pack switched **off**, so the wrong pack doesn't take the sync.

## Fix 2: scan for clear channels (best in a new room)

A scan finds channels nobody else in the building is using. Use it if Fix 1 still gives noise or dropouts.

1. **Switch off every bodypack** (p. 49: packs left on "are detected as unavailable frequencies").
2. On receiver 1: UP/DOWN to **SCAN**, press **SET** (pp. 49–50).
3. Choose the **bank** and press **SET** to start. The receiver shows the next free frequency.
4. Press **SET** to take it, or UP/DOWN to see the next free one. ON/OFF cancels and keeps the old frequency.
5. **Sync pack 1** to receiver 1 (as in Fix 1, step 4), and **leave pack 1 on**.
6. On receiver 2, scan the **same bank**. Pack 1 is on, so the scan skips its frequency. Take a free channel and sync pack 2.

Sennheiser's help article "XSW 2 Scan and Sync" adds a tip: turn the receiver's rear **SQ (squelch) knob down to about 7–8 o'clock**
before scanning, and put it back to **12 o'clock** afterwards. If the scan finds nothing free, raise the squelch and scan again.

## Still crosstalk?

- **Two different banks.** The channels are only free of interference *within one bank*, so put both receivers in the same bank (p. 57).
- **A pack synced to the wrong receiver.** Turn pack 2 off. If receiver 2 still shows signal, or receiver 1 goes quiet, the pair
  is swapped. Sync again, one pair at a time.
- **Noise when a pack is off.** Turn the **SQ knob** clockwise a little. The squelch mutes signals below a threshold (3–28 dBµV,
  pp. 56, 85). Set it too high and the range gets shorter.
- **Antennas.** Angle the two antennas slightly left and right (p. 42). Keep the receivers out of a closed metal rack, unless you
  use the front-antenna kit (GA 2-XSW 2, p. 10).
- **Something else on the air** (another room, a TV transmitter). Run Fix 2 so the scan finds clear channels.

## What the manual doesn't cover

These are general wireless practice, not from Sennheiser's manual, so treat them as **unverified**:

- Keep the two receivers a little apart, and keep each pack a metre or more from the other receiver.
- Don't stand a performer right on top of the receivers.

The manual also has no keypad lock, user bank or minimum MHz spacing. Stick to the bank's preset channels.
